pull.title: gui: Use PSBT v0
pull.body:
This fixes: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36518

There is no test added here for the bump fee PSBT's being v0, since there aren't any existing tests for watch only wallet feebumping in the GUI. If reviewers insist on this I can add it, but I wanted to keep the diff minimal. I have tested this manually.

AFAIU for the external signer stuff it shouldn't matter much whether it's v0 or v2, since users are very unlikely to be using HWI software that doesn't speak v0, but out of caution I've set the external signer PSBT to v0 for the GUI.

_This PR originally took the approach of adding a checkbox, ([davidgumberg/gui/2026-10-15-psbt-gui](https://github.com/davidgumberg/gui/tree/2026-10-15-psbt-gui)), but this was dropped to simplify backporting past string freeze._

_LLM Disclosure: The previous approach was drafted using an LLM, but this branch was written by me. I used an LLM to explore adding a fee bump watchonly GUI test, and decided against it._

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.
I don't think we should be adding any GUI elements for a PR targeting a backport, particularly as it adds strings for translation. We can do v0 only in the GUI I guess.

> We can do v0 only in the GUI I guess.

That seems fine for now if it's easier. There could be a (release) note to use the RPC for v2 when needed.

events.message:
gui: wallet: Use v0 PSBT

PSBTv2 is not very interesting for current GUI users, and defaulting to
it causes issues for existing users. Because this change is a fix, it
only changes the default back instead of adding a checkbox.
refactor: psbt: Don't set a default version for PSBT constructor

rename.from: gui: Make PSBT version toggleable: v0 by default

events.body: I've pushed so that the GUI just returns v0 PSBT's.

Code review f0777e68550cc100ab0341515c5c34bac45fc7a4.

> AFAIU for the external signer stuff it shouldn't matter much whether it's v0 or v2, since users are very unlikely to be using HWI software that doesn't speak v0, but out of caution I've set the external signer PSBT to v0 for the GUI.

I think it's better to consistently use v2 for external signers, both from the GUI and RPC.
